reason: Verified in source and by driving the page. render-b.js:515-519 is the whole of the add branch: it takes root.querySelector('.b-item') and opens the editor on it. Driven at 1440 on ?v=approach&state=owner-flight, pressing "Add a moment" leaves the row count at 7 and opens the editor on demo-audience-item-menu with #b-edit-title pre-filled "Menu tasting at The Orchard"; focus stays on the Add button, and the reversibility bar stays empty. The owner's only creation verb creates nothing, and the panel it opens is the rename panel for someone else's moment. This is not the deliberate inert-text case: it is a real <button> with a data-act, which by the direction's own rule is a promise. It is not covered by the gates: interaction-check.mjs:541-550 only asserts that every button carries a data-act attribute, never that the verb on the face matches the act. One factual correction to the finding, which does not save it: the title input at render-b.js:416 has no handler at all, so typing does not in fact rename the borrowed moment — nothing is written anywhere. That makes the harm different, not smaller: the creation verb is dead AND the editor's title field is dead, so no moment in this direction can be named or created by the owner at all. On the fixture question: creating a NEW EMPTY moment is the owner's own input, not invented fixture content. The brief's rule ("Never placeholder text, never a hand-rolled imitation of the data") governs what the lab SHOWS as the Mara & Finn plan; a blank row the operator makes by pressing a button and then types into is their input, and it starts with nothing in it, so nothing is fabricated. What WOULD breach the rule is seeding the new moment with an invented title ("Bridesmaid dresses", "New moment", a made-up supplier) or shipping a shot with such a row in it. Empty title, input placeholder only, date derived from a fixture.js accessor, and no change to any captured state (owner-flight and owner-editing render before any click, so no frame content moves).
sharpenedFix: Aim it at render-b.js and fix four places, not one. (1) The add branch (l.515): mint an id, push a fixture-shaped record { id, title: "", date, visibility: "shown" } into the list recordFor reads (F.milestones, l.86-88) — without that, recordFor returns undefined and setAway/grabLabel throw on the first date press — then build the row with the same builder measure() uses (l.98) so data-away/data-date/.b-away/.b-date/.b-grab all exist, insert it in date order, call place(measureEl), open the editor on it and focus #b-edit-title empty. Do NOT default the date to "the midpoint between today and the nearest existing moment": that number is invented and can land on top of a neighbour. Use the direction's own derived spacing — the tightest real gap in the fixture, seven days from the measure's data-clock — clamped by the same ceiling setAway already applies (the day itself), so the new row appears above the first existing moment without colliding. (2) Wire the title input (l.416) on input to write record.title, the row's title node and the .b-grab aria-label (grabLabel), or an added moment can never be named and the fix ships a permanently blank row. (3) history and paintUndo (l.283-308) only understand the moved shape { id, title, from, to } — pushing { kind: "add", id } as written would render "Last change: undefined moved NaN days later." Give history entries an explicit kind, branch paintUndo on it ("Last change: a moment was added."), and branch undo() (l.479) to remove the row and its record, restoring focus to the Add button rather than a .b-step that no longer exists. (4) Add the assertion to interaction-check.mjs: pressing Add a moment increases .b-item count by exactly one, leaves every existing title byte-identical, moves focus into #b-edit-title with an empty value, and Ctrl+Z returns the count to its start. Keep the placeholder microcopy on-voice and out of the data ("What is happening?" in the input only).
